correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern opening and first northward segment, including the first joins.
correspondence.finding: No acquired primary source establishes this selected component and its through-links at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.finding: No acquired primary source establishes this selected component and its through-links at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.finding: No acquired primary source establishes this selected component and its through-links at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower northward continuation and successive turns, including all intervening joins.
correspondence.finding: No acquired primary source establishes this selected component and its through-links at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Final northeastern approach and actual selected coastal terminal.
correspondence.finding: ARC403 supplies only regional coastal context; it does not identify the exact selected arriving river or establish the last approach through to the actual terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: headward_opening_and_first_passages
correspondence.finding: The selected southern opening and its first northeastward passages lie in the lake-and-stream country south of the main northward Bérard corridor. CEHQ depicts regional drainage but does not distinguish the chosen initial feeder and every intervening waterbody connection. RG2013-04 does not cover this opening. No source-lake name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: upper_westward_bend_and_joins
correspondence.finding: The selected upper route makes a westward bend before turning north. The regional CEHQ map does not establish the chosen bend and all its waterbody entries, exits and joins. The detailed RG111 project material was not successfully obtained and supplies no evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: middle_northward_lake_stream_chain
correspondence.finding: CEHQ shows the long northward river-and-lake corridor west of the separately labelled Lac Gerido and Compeau drainage. That regional setting supports the Bérard candidate but does not identify each selected middle lake or demonstrate every inter-lake connector and branch. The retained RG2013-04 map lies east of almost all this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: approach_to_berard_lake_setting
correspondence.finding: The regional map distinguishes Lac Bérard and its north–south lake setting south of Tasiujaq. The source does not resolve the entire chosen southern approach or prove each selected lake-arm passage. The lake label is not extended to neighboring unnamed waters.

correspondence.component_scope: lower_lake_and_river_outlet
correspondence.finding: CEHQ labels Lac Bérard and Rivière Bérard along the lower corridor leading toward Tasiujaq. Their ordinary regional arrangement agrees with the selected lower route, but the available cartography does not resolve all selected lake-to-channel and tributary joins before the eastern map edge is crossed.

correspondence.component_scope: terminal_approach_and_actual_terminal
correspondence.finding: RG2013-04 depicts the final winding approach entering the southwestern Lac aux Feuilles shore beside Tasiujaq. CEHQ independently labels the Bérard river and the same receiving lake and settlement. The selected terminal belongs to this Tasiujaq-side inlet, distinct from Baie Sèche to the east. This is ordinary historical corridor correspondence, with no exact mouth vertex, bank or contemporary tidal limit assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastern opening and initial southward feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected beginning and its first westward join have no actually inspected independent detailed source correspondence. A named coastward river cannot identify this initial feeder by itself.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper westward inland sequence and successive joins
correspondence.finding: All selected upper parts were considered. No permitted original map was read that follows these successive inland reaches, their lake or wetland interruptions, and their joining order.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle southwest-turning approach
correspondence.finding: The approach toward the central lake-country reach remains unmatched. Neither a general river name nor fisheries-report bibliographic title establishes this through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Central long westward reach, lake-country passage and southwest connector
correspondence.finding: The chosen long crossing and southwest continuation lack read map or field prose establishing the selected lake entry, internal passage and actual outlet. Tahiryuak/Tahiryuaq was only a bibliographic-discovery lead and is not accepted as a mapped passage identity.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward transition below the central connector
correspondence.finding: The selected southward transition and its downstream join lack ordinary-scale primary-source correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southwestern river and tributary joins
correspondence.finding: ARC403 identifies Kuuk at the coast in this region. Its coastal description does not trace these inland lower-river parts or all of their intervening joins, so these parts remain material-pending.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected coastward terminal
correspondence.finding: ARC403 printed page4-12, paragraph168 explicitly names Kuuk entering Prince Albert Sound in the selected coastal setting and notes alluvial deposition off the mouth. This supplies a bounded named-mouth candidate, but no read detailed map matches the final selected channel and its continuation to the actual selected endpoint. Exact bank or current-flow proof is not being required.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastern opening, northern arc and initial southwestern turn
correspondence.finding: The read study does not depict the chosen upper feeder with enough geographic detail to connect it to the named town-side river. Its general headwater description does not identify this particular opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Long southwestern upper approach
correspondence.finding: The schematic basin map names the Punilla trunk but does not establish every selected upper connection or its joining feeder. No unsupported upper-reach name is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Entry into the north–south town-side corridor
correspondence.finding: The source shows a named Punilla course approaching the town from the north, but its connection back through the selected northeastern approach is not resolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Punilla town-side reach, tributary junction corridor and lagoon approach
correspondence.finding: Figure 1 depicts the north–south Punilla trunk, the Mirihuaca join farther north, and Los Colorados and Las Pitas joining near Antofagasta de la Sierra before the river approaches the lagoon group. The selected middle corridor follows this ordinary geographic sequence. Ancient irrigation channels are separately symbolized and are not substituted for the river.

correspondence.component_scope: Lagoon-group entry and selected continuation
correspondence.finding: The study describes and depicts Punilla reaching the Lagunas de Antofagasta. Its schematic branches and lagoon symbols do not establish which individual basin the selected line traverses or an onward exit to the south.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward continuation beyond the Antofagasta lagoon setting
correspondence.finding: No inspected source shows the selected through-channel from the lagoon group into this southern interval. Regional descriptions of closed basins are insufficient to establish an inter-basin river passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern alluvial and saltflat approach
correspondence.finding: The official inventory establishes a regional landscape of separate closed basins, saltflats and lagoons including Carachi Pampa. It supplies no selected-channel cartography or authorial connection for this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Final approach and actual southern endpoint
correspondence.finding: Carachi Pampa is a supported regional lagoon and salar name. The inspected inventory does not locate the exact selected receiving feature or demonstrate its connection to the upstream selection. It is therefore not accepted as the terminal identification.
